_about: Sonic-grammar fragment (List 30 #296) — production rules on #82, abstract by construction: no character, place, song, or design is imported. R1 carries the owner's spectacle doctrine (2026-10-27): spectacle is per-power-family; List 32 authors the family grammars — #296 founds, List 32 carries.
doctrine: SPECTACLE IS PER-POWER-FAMILY — every character gets their spectacle: lightning, water, strength, rock, earth/ground, speed, aerial (flight, levitation), ghostly/phantom, yokai spirit powers, the paranormal — each family with its own staging grammar. Speed is one family among them, with no rank above the others. (Owner ruling, 2026-10-27.)
list32_pointer: The deep per-family build is List 32's (#307 spectacle doctrine + per-family packages). A family grammar governs its family; if one disagrees with a rule here, this package is corrected by citation — only R1 binds List 32, by the owner's ruling.

rules.name: spectacle per family
rules.rule: a scene stages a character's power in THAT power family's grammar (List 32) — camera, sound (#215/#51), environmental answer; spectacle shows what a power is LIKE, never how strong it is
rules.test: a child can say which power it was with the sound off and no names spoken

rules.name: zone variety as episode grammar
rules.rule: each #82 arc carries a zone idea line (one dominant visual idea, in the #50 colour script before boards open); consecutive arcs never share one
rules.test: a place is describable in one sentence by a child who saw it once

rules.name: the mirror-rival structure
rules.rule: a lead's dark double is staged in the lead's family grammar INVERTED (same family, reversed register); the episode's turn is one borrowing the other's grammar; homes: List 29 anti-hero line + #131 register
rules.test: in a shared scene, a board can say which grammar is whose

rules.name: attitude is staging, not dialogue
rules.rule: #120/#82 beats carry an attitude note per principal — what staging must make undeniable before their first line; entrances are events; competence is shown first
rules.test: the character reads correctly in a silent cut

rules.name: music identity (leitmotif discipline)
rules.rule: a theme registry (production data, beside #72/#215): principals, power families, major places may hold a motif — first full statement is an episode event; thereafter varied, never merely repeated; assigned sparingly

voice_law_split: humans carry attitude in staging AND speech; creatures stay cries-only — a Mochi's attitude is posture, timing, cry colour (#155), never words or name-saying
